A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SparseVLM study. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V3 reports original image and video benchmark results, token-selection and recycling ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: V4 retains original image experiments and ablations and reports revised video results in Table 3, alongside the retained appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The described procedure retains text-rater selection, attention-based visual significance estimation, rank-adaptive pruning, and token clustering and reconstruction. The appendix FlashAttention procedure is also unchanged.

E1.justification: The same image benchmarks, four video-QA benchmarks, and qualitative scenarios are retained. The newly specified video sample count does not introduce a new task, domain, or test scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain ToMe, FastV, PDrop, and the same appendix comparison curves. PDrop's publication label changes only. V4 Figure 10's caption mentions random sparsification, but its unchanged legend and curves still identify FastV; this does not establish a comparator addition.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 and Table 3 change the reported retained video-token budget from 198 to 194 for both SparseVLM and FastV, with pruning changing from 90.3% to 90.5%. The newly disclosed first-1,000-samples rule does not establish that the sample selection changed.

E4.justification: Figure 5's text-rater ablation, Table 4's recycling ablation, qualitative examples, and appendix efficiency trade-offs retain their evidence. V3 Figures 9–11 become v4 Figures 8–10 without changes to their plotted analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. The added GPT scores are evaluation outcomes, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 3 and Section 4.2 substantially replace the four-benchmark video results. SparseVLM/FastV mean relative accuracies change from 86.5%/52.1% to 95.0%/80.3%; SparseVLM's TGIF accuracy changes from 44.7 to 14.9 and MSRVTT accuracy from 31.0 to 56.1. Per-benchmark GPT scores and raw averages are added. These are revised results under different reported token budgets, not established same-setting performance gains. Image results and ablations remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(11), the FlashAttention mathematics, and the detailed FLOPs derivations are retained. V3 Appendices A.2–A.3 become v4 Appendices B–C without substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The central training-free, text-guided sparsification contributions remain intact. The introduction and conclusion narrow the quantified video advantage over FastV from 34.4 to 14.7 percentage points. The abstract also removes its specific LLaVA efficiency-and-accuracy example.

C2.justification: The explanations of text guidance, information preservation through recycling, video applicability, and deployment benefits retain their substantive meaning. No new mechanism explanation, failure condition, or substantive limitation is introduced.

D1.justification: V4 Section 4.2 newly specifies evaluation on the first 1,000 samples of each video benchmark, following FastV's setup. V3 leaves that selection unspecified. Hardware, software versions, inference implementation descriptions, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds citations to LLaVA-PruMerge, VideoLLM-MoD, the consistency study, and FreeKD, while removing the GPT-4 technical report and DeepSeek LLM references. The central research positioning remains stable; numerous other reference edits merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: V4 makes limited prose edits, updates affiliations and conference information, and adds acknowledgments. Appendix subsections A.1–A.8 become sections A–H, with efficiency analysis placed before additional visualizations. Most scientific exposition remains verbatim.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains paired accuracy/score columns and a redesigned average display. Table 2 and several appendix figures move; the efficiency figures precede the qualitative examples, and Figure 7 follows its explanatory text. Captions are edited, but all figure graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 improves reporting transparency by specifying the video sample-selection rule and adding raw GPT scores that make its aggregate score comparisons checkable. The gains are limited by new errors: Table 3 gives FastV's TGIF score difference as -0.34 although 2.29 minus 2.54 is -0.25, and Figure 10's caption misidentifies a comparator. The added documentation and inspectable results support a limited net improvement despite these defects.
